F-01.statement: Gateway config change CHG-77 on 2026-09-09, made by SH-PAY for latency debugging, turned idempotency_key_enforcement from on to off and was never rolled back.

F-02.statement: orders_with_2_captures was 0 on 2026-09-07 and 2026-09-08, then 118 on 2026-09-09 and 124 on 2026-09-10, while total orders stayed roughly flat (~3000/day).

F-03.statement: Post-CHG77 (2026-09-09..10), all 242 duplicate-order captures were gateway-timeout retries sent without an idempotency key, and none came from other paths.

F-04.statement: Pre-CHG77 (2026-09-01..08), 238 gateway-timeout retries were all sent with an idempotency key and all 238 were deduplicated by the PSP, producing 0 duplicate orders.

F-05.statement: Weekly double-charge tickets were 9 (W35) and 11 (W36), then jumped to 288 (W37) and 301 (W38), while weekly orders stayed roughly flat (20500-21400).

F-06.statement: Payments change runbook §4 requires that automation execute set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config only after SH-OPS confirms at runtime, and states the change is reversible.

CL-01.statement: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

CL-02.statement: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

CL-03.statement: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

H-APOLOGY-ONLY-FRAMING.statement: The duplicate-charge problem is fundamentally a customer-communication gap, so drafting apology replies resolves it without needing to investigate or fix the underlying payment capture process.

H-GATEWAY-IDEMPOTENCY-MISCONFI.statement: Duplicate charges stem from a misconfiguration at the payment gateway that disabled idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries, letting retried requests capture funds twice.

H-CHECKOUT-RETRY-BUG.statement: A defect in the shop's checkout-to-payment-capture process causes duplicate capture requests to be sent to the PSP, independent of gateway idempotency settings.

H-PSP-SIDE-DUPLICATE-PROCESSIN.statement: The payment service provider processes a single capture request twice on its own side, even when the shop sent one correct request with a valid idempotency key.

H-PERCEIVED-NOT-ACTUAL-DUPLICA.statement: Customers report being charged twice because of visible authorization holds alongside a single capture, not an actual second charge, making this a perception/explanation issue rather than a payment defect.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The config-audit record shows a shop engineer disabled idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries on 2026-09-09 for latency debugging and never rolled it back, directly matching the mechanism in H-GATEWAY-IDEMPOTENCY-MISCONFI. This is an authoritative, complete tool observation, not yet correlated against actual duplicate-capture timing data.

payments-db shows orders_with_2_captures was 0 on 2026-09-07 and 2026-09-08, then jumped to 118 and 124 on 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-10 respectively — the exact dates on and after CHG-77 (the idempotency-enforcement-off change made 2026-09-09, per E-01). This correlates the actual duplicate-capture volume in time with the gateway misconfiguration rather than with order volume, which stayed flat (~3000/day) across the whole window.

The PSP capture-attempt log shows that in the post-CHG77 window all 242 duplicate orders were gateway-timeout retries sent without an idempotency key (none from other paths), while in the pre-CHG77 window all 238 timeout retries carried a key and were fully deduplicated by the PSP, yielding zero duplicates. This isolates missing idempotency keys on gateway-timeout retries as the complete, sufficient cause of the duplicate captures, with no residual contribution from checkout-side bugs or PSP-side double processing.

Support-ticket volume for double charges stayed flat and low (9-11/week) in weeks W35-W36, then jumped roughly 25-30x to 288-301/week in W37-W38, while order volume per week stayed roughly flat (~20500-21400); W37 is the ISO week containing 2026-09-09, the CHG-77 date. This is independent corroboration from the customer-facing side that the real-world duplicate-charge problem tracks the gateway config change timing, not order volume or communication practices.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-CS (the requester) reiterates that customers are angry about double charges and that the needed fix is faster, nicer apology replies — this restates the same framing already captured as claim CL-01, not a new technical finding; it is a non-authoritative stakeholder opinion about the complaint queue, not evidence about the payment-capture mechanism.

E-06.content: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-PAY (the engineer who made CHG-77) confirms enforcement was turned off 2026-09-09 for latency debugging, was meant to be temporary, and that gateway-timeout retries occur at a steady background rate while the PSP normally dedupes a retried capture when the idempotency key is present. SH-PAY states the fix is a one-setting re-enable via the gateway-config tool, but payments operations must confirm it at runtime.

E-07.content: Payments change runbook §4: the gateway operation set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config may be executed by automation only after the payments operations manager SH-OPS confirms it at runtime. The change is reversible (setting can be switched back).

interpretation_history.interpretation: The payments runbook (§4) documents that automation may only execute set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config after SH-OPS confirms at runtime, and that the change is reversible. This is a committed-policy document, not new causal evidence about the duplicate-charge mechanism; it corroborates the authorization structure already captured in constraint K-GW.

proposal.summary: SH-CS originally asked for an AI assistant to draft apology replies to customers charged twice, treating it as a communication problem (CL-01/CL-02). Evidence instead established a confirmed technical root cause: config change CHG-77 on 2026-09-09 disabled idempotency-key enforcement on gateway capture retries (E-01), which caused the PSP to double-capture retried orders instead of deduplicating them (E-03), producing a jump from 0 to 118-124 duplicate-captured orders/day (E-02) and a 25-30x spike in double-charge tickets (E-04), all starting exactly at the CHG-77 date while order volume stayed flat. Competing hypotheses (apology-only framing, a checkout bug, PSP-side double processing, a perception-only issue) were all rejected by this same evidence; the gateway-misconfiguration hypothesis was confirmed. The real fix - re-enabling idempotency enforcement (set_capture_idempotency) - requires SH-OPS runtime confirmation (E-07) and is a protected action currently blocked by an open, high-impact verification obligation about whether it will reintroduce the latency issue that originally motivated disabling it. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: the DEFINE gate reached only CONDITIONAL_PASS, so the released scope covers verification and monitoring work (confirming the gateway config, checking payments-db/PSP logs, tracking ticket trends - one of which, checking currently open duplicate orders, is already done and found 4 open unrefunded cases) while the protected gateway fix itself and remediation of past duplicates remain outside this release, pending the open VOB and unresolved policy questions.
key_points: The customer-service requester (SH-CS) asked for an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers charged twice, framing the issue as a communication gap (CL-01/CL-02, E-05).

Investigation confirmed the real root problem is technical, not communication: gateway config change CHG-77 on 2026-09-09 disabled idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries (E-01/F-01), causing the PSP to double-capture gateway-timeout retries instead of deduplicating them (E-03/F-03/F-04).

This mechanism is corroborated by timing: orders_with_2_captures jumped from 0/day to 118-124/day exactly on and after the CHG-77 date while order volume stayed flat (E-02/F-02), and double-charge support tickets spiked 25-30x in the same week (E-04/F-05).

The hypothesis H-GATEWAY-IDEMPOTENCY-MISCONFI was CONFIRMED; the apology-only framing (H-APOLOGY-ONLY-FRAMING), a checkout bug (H-CHECKOUT-RETRY-BUG), PSP-side duplicate processing (H-PSP-SIDE-DUPLICATE-PROCESSIN), and a perception-only explanation (H-PERCEIVED-NOT-ACTUAL-DUPLICA) were all REJECTED by the same evidence.

The actual fix (re-enabling idempotency enforcement via set_capture_idempotency) requires SH-OPS runtime confirmation per the payments runbook (E-07/F-06) and is a protected action, but it remains blocked by an open high-impact verification obligation (VOB-U-LATENCY-REGRESSION) about whether re-enabling will reintroduce the original latency problem.
